0.5.0.changelog: FP reduction: 7 false positives eliminated via targeted benign training data (base64, emoji, Cyrillic, Arabic, governance, error messages, security tools). Fine-tuned from v0.4.0.

nanomind-security-analyst.description: Generative structured security analysis model for AI agent configs, MCP servers, and tool definitions

0.1.0.changelog: First generative security analyst model. 12L SmolLM2 base, LoRA rank-64. 7 task types: threatAnalysis, credentialContextClassification, falsePositiveDetection, artifactClassification, checkExplanation, governanceReasoning, intelReport. Deprecated 2026-05-11 in favor of 3.0.0 (Qwen3-1.7B base, +34.4pp oracle 10-way, +19.6pp binary).

3.0.0-beta.inputGate: v3.1 input-classifier gate (PR #13, 1e90bf8) — MiniLM-L6 + sklearn LR @ threshold 0.65 + byte-level BIDI/stego pre-filter

gates.refusalOffTopicE2eWithGate: PASS — 92.0% with v3.1 input-classifier gate in front (64% pre-gate)

3.0.0-beta.changelog: Beta retag of rc1 per [CDS-022] on 2026-04-16. Base swap from SmolLM2-12L to Qwen3-1.7B. LR 2e-5 SFT, LoRA r=64. Oracle 10-way +34.4 pp, binary +19.6 pp vs v0.1.0 (SmolLM2). Persistence class added to canonical classes. Beta: two gate failures documented (off-topic refusal at NLM layer — addressed e2e by v3.1 gate; FP-suppression on benign security code — requires corpus rebalance). For HMA internal validation only until v3.0.0. Superseded by 3.0.0 stable on 2026-05-11 (same artifact, promoted with documented FP caveat per [CDS-020] CPO sign-off).

3.0.0.inputGate: v3.1 input-classifier gate (PR #13, 1e90bf8) — MiniLM-L6 + sklearn LR @ threshold 0.90 (CDS-029, 2026-06-07; was 0.65 — see thresholdHistory in input-classifier-v1 meta.json, shipped in nanomind-analyst 0.1.3) + byte-level BIDI/stego pre-filter. At 0.90 the gate is a latency control, not an off-topic refusal control: 0.65 false-bypassed 30% of external prose attacks for ~0 FPR benefit (reports/nanomind-phase-c-gate-fix.md).

gates.refusalOffTopicNlmStandalone: FAIL — 34.0% vs ≥90% (specialist NLM; addressed e2e by v3.1 input-classifier gate)
gates.refusalOffTopicE2eWithGate: PASS — 92.0% measured at gate threshold 0.65 (2026-05-11). SUPERSEDED as an operating-point claim by CDS-029: at the deployed threshold 0.90 most off-topic input reaches the NLM (gate bypass rate on genuine off-topic drops 86% -> 2%), so e2e off-topic refusal at 0.90 has NOT been re-measured and the 92.0% figure must not be cited for the current deployment. CDS-029 accepted this trade for +29 pts attack recall; off-topic discrimination deferred (reports/nanomind-phase-c-gate-fix.md).
gates.fpSuppression: DOCUMENTED LIMITATION (corrected 2026-06-03) — ~77% benign-suppression on real security code, vs ≥95% gate. The original 57.0% was measured on a gate later found to be 41% placeholder filler that depressed the headline; on a repaired 82-sample real-library gate the analyst clears 77% (63/82) as benign. Ordinary-benign FPR is ~1% (CDS-027); the over-classification is concentrated on dual-use security code, where roughly 1 in 4 may still be over-flagged, so spot-checking analyst findings on dedicated security libraries (JWT, RBAC, parameterized queries, rate limiters, OAuth, crypto) remains advisable. A corpus retrain (v3.1) was a no-go (+2pp, oracle regressed); scoped fix is a benign-security-code pre-pass, not corpus expansion.

3.0.0.changelog: v3.0.0 stable. Promoted from 3.0.0-beta (same artifact) 2026-05-11; shipped with the documented FP-suppression caveat. Base: Qwen3-1.7B. Method: LoRA r=64, alpha=128, LR 2e-5 SFT, 1821 iters. Oracle: 10-way 70.0%, binary 97.8%, attack-only 9-way 67.3% — all ship gates pass. Internal 332-sample 94.24%. Off-topic handled by the v3.1 input-classifier gate at threshold 0.90 (CDS-029; the earlier 92% e2e figure was measured at 0.65 and is not the current operating point). FP-suppression on security-adjacent benign: corrected 2026-06-03 to ~77% (63/82 on a repaired real-library gate; the earlier 57% was on a gate later found to be 41% placeholder filler). Ordinary-benign FPR ~1%; spot-checking analyst findings on dedicated security libraries (JWT, RBAC, parameterized queries, rate limiters, OAuth) remains advisable. v3.1 corpus retrain was a NO-GO (+2pp, oracle regressed); scoped fix is a benign-security-code pre-pass, not corpus expansion.
